page: Amazon Web Services r9g.12xlarge is an ARM-based, memory-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 processors running on the Nitro hypervisor. The configuration features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at 3.3 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. It provides 384.0 GB of memory, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB per core. The cache architecture includes 64 KB L1 data cache per core, 2 MB L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 25 Gbps. There is no bundled local storage or integrated GPU, requiring workloads to rely on remote storage solutions such as Amazon EBS.

Benchmark results highlight strong parallel processing and cache-level throughput. Multi-core CPU operations scored 95,877.59 in stress-ng tests, ranking in the top 25%, while single-core performance registered at 1,982.88. Cached read operations reached 6,443.87 GB/sec, contrasting with uncached block bandwidth of 186.67 GB/sec for reads and 84.53 GB/sec for writes. The instance excels in compression and memory-centric throughput, achieving 579.62 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, 125.22 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads, and 156.54 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks, all placing in the top decile.

The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio provides resource efficiency for workloads requiring large memory footprints without overprovisioning excess compute cores. Because each vCPU represents a dedicated physical core, the architecture delivers consistent performance free from hyperthreading contention. A primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of local instance storage, making I/O performance dependent on network-attached storage or in-memory operations.

AWS r9g.12xlarge is suited for in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, high-throughput web serving, real-time analytics engines, and data transformation jobs such as decompression or ETL pipelines.

Designed with an 8:1 memory-to-core allocation, it delivers 25 Gbps baseline networking and includes no local storage or GPU hardware. The instance exhibits exceptional memory-intensive throughput, reaching 125.22 million Redis SET operations per second, 579.62 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and 6,443.87 GB/sec in small-block cached memory reads. Multi-core performance reaches 95,877.59 in stress-ng evaluations. By eliminating thread contention with single-threaded physical cores, r9g.12xlarge offers balanced compute and high memory density for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, data processing pipelines, and high-concurrency web tiers.
